name: China
summary: The world's manufacturing superpower and principal strategic competitor to the United States. China dominates critical-mineral processing and clean-tech supply chains, is rapidly expanding its navy and nuclear arsenal, and seeks unification with Taiwan.
strategicInterests: Unification with Taiwan and deterrence of US intervention
Consolidate claims in the South and East China Seas
Technological self-reliance against US export controls
Leverage over critical minerals (rare earths, gallium, graphite)
Belt and Road and leadership of the Global South

name: Japan
summary: A technological and financial powerhouse and the linchpin US ally in Asia, undertaking its largest defence build-up since 1945. Tokyo is doubling defence spending to 2% of GDP and acquiring counterstrike missiles to deter China and North Korea.
strategicInterests: Deter Chinese coercion around the Senkakus and Taiwan
Counter North Korean missile threats
Strengthen the US alliance and networks with Australia, the Philippines and the UK
Economic security: semiconductors and supply-chain resilience
Energy security for a resource-poor economy

government.notes: Japan's first female prime minister, in office since October 2025.

name: South Korea
summary: An advanced manufacturing economy at the heart of global memory-chip, battery and shipbuilding supply chains, living under constant threat from North Korea. Political turmoil after the December 2024 martial-law declaration ended with Lee Jae-myung's election in June 2025.
strategicInterests: Deterrence of North Korea under the US alliance
Stable trade with both China and the United States
Defence exports (tanks, howitzers, fighters)
Nuclear-powered submarine programme

resources.name: Shipbuilding

name: North Korea
summary: A hereditary totalitarian state with a growing nuclear arsenal and ICBMs. Its 2024 mutual-defence treaty with Russia — and the deployment of troops to fight for Russia — has given Pyongyang cash, technology and relief from diplomatic isolation.
strategicInterests: Regime survival and recognition as a nuclear-weapon state
Military-technical cooperation with Russia
Sanctions evasion, including large-scale crypto theft
Treat South Korea as a separate, hostile state (doctrine since 2024)

name: Taiwan
summary: A self-governing democracy claimed by Beijing, producing the vast majority of the world's most advanced semiconductors. Mounting Chinese military pressure makes the Taiwan Strait the most consequential flashpoint in the Indo-Pacific.
strategicInterests: Deter invasion or blockade through asymmetric defence
Sustain US arms sales and political support
Preserve its semiconductor edge (the 'silicon shield')
Energy resilience for an import-dependent grid
International space and diplomatic allies

capabilities: HIMARS, Harpoon coastal defence and drones

name: India
summary: The world's most populous country and fastest-growing major economy, pursuing 'strategic autonomy' between the West, Russia and the Global South. India faces an unresolved border with China and fought a brief conflict with Pakistan in May 2025.

Deter cross-border terrorism from Pakistan
Primacy in the Indian Ocean region
Manufacturing growth and technology partnerships

name: Pakistan
summary: A nuclear-armed state where the military holds decisive power. Pakistan depends on IMF support, is China's closest partner in South Asia, signed a mutual defence pact with Saudi Arabia in 2025 and faces rising militancy on its Afghan border.

Counter TTP and Baloch insurgencies
Economic stabilisation under the IMF programme
